https://www.dw.com/en/sudan-us-proposes-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JKwq Observers say weaponry is getting more sophisticated on both sides of the conflict in Sudan [FILE: Aug 30, 2023] Image: AFP Advertisement The United States on Monday proposed expanding an existing UN arms embargo for Darfur to cover all of Sudan . The proposal was put forth by US Envoy Massad Boulos during a UN Security Council meeting in New York. "The brutality of the war waged by the Rapid Support Forces [RSF] and the Sudanese Armed Forces has discredited their claims to be legitimate governors of the Sudanese people," said Boulos, who warned that "external financial and military support is fueling the conflict and risks drawing neighboring states deeper into war." Boulos said the US wants to expand the embargo geographically as well as materially in order to cover unmanned aerial vehicles and related technologies . Moreover, the US plan would see the number of experts monitoring the embargo increased. The Darfur embargo has been in place for two decades and will expire on September 12, 2026, if not amended or renewed. An expansion would require a Security Council vote. Sudan wants 'technical extension' but warns against hampering army Sudan's UN envoy urged members to endorse a "technical extension" of the existing embargo while warning against changes that would hamper the army. "Sudan suffers the most from weapons and their illegal flow. However, expanding such a sanctions regime will weaken the protection of civilians," said Al-Harith Idriss al-Harith Mohamed. Russia , which holds veto powers in the Security Council, has voiced skepticism over changes to the existing deal, saying that expanding the embargo could impact the Sudanese army's effectiveness. "Sophisticated weaponry," she said, "continues to point to ongoing external support to both parties." The UN's humanitarian chief, Tom Fletcher, also made note of the fact that, "in recent weeks, fighting in Sudan has been characterized by the heavy use of drones and localized ground combat in areas less affected by rainy season conditions." The war in Sudan , now in its fourth year, has killed tens of thousands and displaced millions of civilians. While Sudan's army holds sway in the country's central and eastern regions, western and parts of southern Darfur are under control of rival Rapid Support Forces . Darfur, a vast western region the size of France, has seen some of the worst violence of the conflict, with repeated attacks on displacement camps and ethnic massacres that kill thousands at a time . https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/30/came.text: A Cameroonian group known as "Bring Back Our Sons and Brothers" is calling on both Russia and Cameroon to work together to dismantle covert recruitment networks that have been enlisting Cameroonians into the Russian army to fight in Moscow's invasion of Ukraine.The collective organised a peaceful march to the Russian Embassy on Wednesday as Cameroonians took to the streets of the country's capital, Yaoundé, to protest such schemes."This march aims to draw the attention of two friendly nations - Russia and Cameroon - urging them to do everything in their power to dismantle the clandestine network that continues to drain Cameroon of its sons," Paul Sylvain Yede, one of the group's cofounders, said.According to a report by the collective "All Eyes on Wagner," at least 1,417 Africans have been recruited into the ranks of the Russian military, with more than 300 reported dead.Lured by the promise of employment in Russia, these young men have instead found themselves thrust onto the front lines in Ukraine, where Russian forces launched a full-scale invasion in February 2022.Catherine Djock has been waiting for news of her husband for the best part of a year after he travelled to Russia to take up what he thought would be work in a kitchen."For nine months, I have had no information about my husband’s situation - whether he is alive or not. I cannot accept that he is dead, as I have not seen his body; therefore, I believe he is still alive," she said."If he is alive, I want Russia to bring my husband back to me. He was supposed to work as a cook, but upon his arrival, he ended up on the front lines. I want the truth about my husband. That is why I have come out today."Ngong San Djombi, the father of a victim, added: "I lost a son - the youngest of my five children. I demand that my son be returned to me, regardless of his condition - even if he is disabled. I cannot accept being told he is gone when I haven’t seen his body. I have refused to hold a funeral; I have simply prayed."
